text:
Maya: kicking off canary + network sanity for sea4. goal is a tight gate: canary must pass 95% token throughput at 50ms p50, p99 < 350ms, no packet drops on inter-rack path. running today at 08:00 UTC. @oncall-eng-infra please shadow. :eyes:

Jin: on it. I pushed the canary job to the dedicated pool (gpu-pool-sea4-canary), image redwood/infer:stable-2026-03-18. running the short load profile now (100 small sessions). will paste results.

ops-bot: Deploy started: canary/gpu-pool-sea4-canary @ 2026-03-18T08:02:10Z. CI job 4482 -> rolling to 3 nodes.

Jin: quick health check command:```curl -sS http://canary-sea4.internal/health | jq .``` output:```{
  "status": "ok",
  "gpus": 3,
  "kv_cache_hit": 0.72,
  "open_requests": 2
}``` no errors. latency probe (p50/p95/p99): 42ms / 220ms / 310ms. 95% sessions completed.

Sergio: seeing intermittent UDP/MTU fragmentation on rack-2 -> rack-3 path. tcpdump shows ICMP frag-needed for 1500->1400 mismatch. snippet:```13:42:17.123456 IP hostA > hostB: Frag needed and DF set (MTU 1400)``` This is dropping large model sync messages occasionally which correlates with a small number of failed KV syncs.

Priya: ack. MTU mismatch could also be from the transit switch config not matching host jumbo config. quick workaround: reduce jumbo on hosts to 1400 for canary or enable PMTU blackhole timeout. Which do you prefer?

Jin: for an easy rollback, I'll patch the canary DaemonSet to set net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=0 temporarily and add iptables rule to clamp MSS:```iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu``` applying to nodes in gpu-pool-sea4-canary. rolling now.

Maya: do that. also add this to the checklist under "network gating" with a follow-up ticket to reconcile switch+host MTU.

Jin: applied. rerunning load. new latency: 45ms / 230ms / 295ms. packet drop counters zeroed. KV sync failures dropped to 0 in 1k syncs.

Sergio: confirmed at switch side there was an inconsistent MTU on transit L3. created NET-SEA4-12 to track permanent fix. tagging networking.

Priya: aside from network, we should validate GPU capacity / scheduling: baseline utilization target for canary is < 60% util on steady-state 1x baseline. observed GPU util ~55% with current config. pods pending occasionally due to affinity on rack-1. recommendation: relax rack-affinity for canary only and keep production affinity strict.

Jin: I relaxed anti-affinity for canary. pending pods scheduled. bump in ephemeral egress cost noted but negligible for canary.

Maya: cost note - we evaluated using 3 x A100-80G vs 6 x A10s; for initial canary A10 family has too high variance. we'll keep A100s for canary and re-evaluate before Dedicated commit. add to handoff doc: "Cost tradeoff: A100 canary for stable metrics; target Dedicated pools may use mixed families after validation."

Priya: SLO gate checklist I'm adding here: 
- control plane health: k8s nodes Ready >= 99%
- API latency: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 375ms
- no packet loss on inter-rack paths during 15m window
- KV sync error rate < 0.1%
- GPU util (canary) between 40-65%
- autoscaler cooldown exercised (scale up + down) at least once
- rollout canary must not cause >1% elevated latency in adjacent clusters

Sergio: adding network probes to monitoring: icmp mtudetect, TCP MSS clamp presence, and SNMP interface MTU. will wire alerts if mismatch > 0.

ops-bot: Canary job completed: 1000 sessions, pass: 973, fail: 27. Check failures: 21 transient connection resets (MTU issue resolved), 6 auth token timeouts (service-rate-limit bump).

Jin: after fixes rerun: 1000 sessions pass: 997 fail: 3. Investigating the 3 timeouts (likely ephemeral auth reissuance race).

Maya: handoff to oncall: @oncall-eng-infra — canary stable enough for limited traffic. next steps: escalate NET-SEA4-12 to priority-high, schedule rack MTU reconciliation during maintenance window, open Dedicated sizing RFC with cost delta. Also create a rollback snapshot for the canary image.

oncall-eng-infra: acknowledged. I'll watch the next 2 hours and escalate to networking if NET-SEA4-12 shows regressions. added followups to playbook: "sea4-canary-postmortem" and "sea4-mtu-remediation". :white_check_mark:

Maya: thanks everyone. putting final checklist tick in the runbook: network clamp applied, canary pass thresholds met, GPU util ok, cost note captured. moving to controlled ramp to 10% traffic for next 24h.

Jin: leaving the commands used in thread for quick repro:```kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/canary-proxy && watch -n 5 'kubectl top pod -n infra | head -n 10'```

Sergio: logs attached to NET-SEA4-12. ping @Priya for any follow-ups on autoscaler tuning.

Priya: I'll schedule autoscaler test tomorrow 09:00 UTC and post the results here.

Maya: good. closing this thread for active changes. archival note: add this thread link to the central bring-up runbook under sea4: https://confluence.internal/redwood/sea4-bringup (internal). :lock:
